newsitem.title: UK: Moody's assigns BPI-SGPS, Banco Fonsecas ratings.
newsitem.headline: Moody's assigns BPI-SGPS, Banco Fonsecas ratings.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service on Friday issued the following statement.

Moody's Investors Service assigned A2/Prime-1 deposit ratings and a financial strength rating of C to Banco Fonsecas e Burnay, S.A. (BFB) and A3 counterparty rating to BPI-SGPS, S.A. BFB is 100% owned by BPI-SGPS, S.A., the holding company of the Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) group. In assigning the ratings, Moody's cited BFB's improving asset quality, ample liquidity, and good profitability -- along with its growing retail banking franchise in Portugal. The rating also reflects the bank's relatively high cost structure.

BFB is the retail banking arm of the BPI group. The bank has 5% market share in customer savings and 4% in loans. Since its acquisition in the early 1990s by BPI, BFB has gone through a major restructuring in which the BPI group has committed significant management and financial resources to its turnaround. However, despite the significant improvement in BFB's fundamentals, the bank's cost structure remains heavy and the net positive effects of the bank's cost cutting program will take some time to be reflected in its financial performan while low interest rates, low inflation, increasing savings disintermediation and growing competition are likely continue to pressure downwards Portuguese banks' recurring earning profitability.

During the past few years the BPI group has embarked on a growth strategy that aims at strengthening its retail domestic banking position. According to Moody's, this strategy that is being accomplished by a series of bank acquisitions (BFB and more recently Banco de Fomento e Exterior, S.A.) and by the opening of new branches, has had so far a negative effect on BPI's cost structure and presents strategic and operational challenges for management. Longer-term however, the group should benefit from enhanced recurring revenues and from better operational efficiencies. The rating agency also added that it expects BPI to maintain a growth and development strategy that would not increase the risk profile of its business and balance sheet.
Banco Fonsecas e Burnay, S.A., with assets of PtE. 1 trillion (USD 7 billion) in June 1996, is headquartered in Lisboa, Portugal.
BPI - SGPS, with assets of PtE 100 billion (USD 658 million) in June 1996, is headquartered in Porto, Portugal.
